messages:
emily: Hi team, quick one 164f. My spouse and I are moving from CA to OR next week and she has an ongoing outpatient therapy plan. How do we confirm which therapists are in-network in OR and whether her existing provider can bill as in-network (they're out-of-state)? Appointment next Wed and we need continuity.

linda (Benefits): Congrats on the move! Two parts: 1) Use the carrier provider search and filter by zip + "in-network"; 2) for continuity of care with an out-of-state provider, we can submit a continuity of care exception / transitional care request if the provider accepts the plan. Do you have the current therapist's NPI and plan name?

emily: Plan: Redwood Plus PPO. Therapist is Dr. Ana Ruiz, NPI 1234567890, currently licensed in CA only. Will the carrier allow telehealth out-of-state or pay for transition visits?

david (People Ops): PPOs usually have more flexibility than HMOs for out-of-network, but coverage out-of-state varies. Ask the carrier about telehealth licensing rules and whether they'd honor a continuity exception while she finishes treatment.

benefits-bot: Automated tip    - Provider search: https://www.carriercare.com/providers. Customer service: 1-800-555-0199 (press 3 for continuity/claims). Submit docs: Claims > Continuity/Transitional Care.

linda (Benefits): I'll open a case with the carrier. Emily, please upload the last 3 visit notes, treatment plan, and the therapist's contact info to the portal under "Continuity Requests" so we can request an exception. If the provider agrees to accept the plan's allowed amount and files as in-network, that helps.

emily: Uploaded the visit notes and treatment plan, plus Dr. Ruiz email (ana@careclinic.example). Her clinic says they can register as an in-network provider but it takes 20 weeks.

karen (People Ops): Ping if they need a prior auth form filled by the therapist. Also check EAP - depending on the plan, short-term sessions might be covered immediately through our Employee Assistance Program while the exception is processed.

linda (Benefits): Good point. EAP can cover up to 6 sessions without claims. I'll include EAP referral in the carrier escalation. Opening case now  Case created: C-992. Carrier estimated response 3-5 business days but sometimes faster for active treatment.

emily: Appointment scheduled for next Wed 10:00AM local. If carrier response is slow, can we get pre-approval to pay and request reimbursement?

linda (Benefits): Yes you can pay upfront and submit an urgent out-of-network claim. Keep itemized receipt and payment proof. We'll flag it urgent once we have the case number. If they deny, we escalate through benefits appeals.

david (People Ops): Also note portability: if Dr. Ruiz can offer telehealth licensed to OR or a local supervised provider can continue sessions, that may be smoother. We can help coordinate referrals if needed.

emily: Thanks all. One last q: does continuity exception preserve copay vs coinsurance? The carrier fee schedule determines that, right?

linda (Benefits): Correct  exceptions typically make the provider in-network for a limited time or allow the plan to pay as if in-network; specifics depend on carrier decision. We'll share the carrier's determination and details about patient cost responsibility when the case returns.

benefits-bot: Automated update  Continuity case C-992 logged. Next update expected by 2026-03-30.

emily: Appreciate it. I'll keep the appt and let you know if the clinic asks for anything else. :pray:
